Count lines of R code in packages

Source: R/pkg_lines.R
pkg_lines.Rd

Analyse the R source files (.R and .r) in R/, tests/ and data-raw/ of one or more packages and count their lines, broken down two ways: by type (code, comment, roxygen, blank) and by location (R/, tests/, elsewhere).

Usage

pkg_lines(
  path = ".",
  include_ignored = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE,
  cache = c("session", "persistent", "none")
)

Arguments

path

A character vector of packages. Each element is one of:

  • A local folder, such as "." or "~/code/mypkg". Use "local::path" to be explicit.

  • A GitHub repository, such as "r-lib/cli" or a github.com URL. Add @ref for a branch, tag or commit ("r-lib/cli@v3.6.0"). For a package in a subfolder, use the github:: prefix: "github::owner/repo/subdir".

  • A CRAN package, such as "desc". Add @version for an older release ("cran::desc@1.4.0"). Archived packages are supported.

Without a prefix, existing local folders take precedence, then "owner/repo" is treated as GitHub and a bare name as CRAN. A path that does not exist (e.g. "./mypkg") is an error, not a GitHub request.

include_ignored

If TRUE, also analyse files matched by the package's .Rbuildignore. Version-control folders and R's built-in build exclusions are always skipped.

quiet

If TRUE, suppress progress messages.

cache

Where to keep downloaded GitHub and CRAN packages:

  • "session" (default): a temporary folder, removed when R closes.

  • "persistent": a user cache folder kept across R sessions. Only fixed versions are stored there: CRAN releases and GitHub refs that look like a commit SHA or a version tag ("owner/repo@v1.2.0"). Requests that can change over time (no ref, or a branch) always fetch the latest code and use the session cache instead.

  • "none": always download afresh.

Use pkg_cache_clear() to empty a cache.

Value

A pkginspectr_tbl with one row per package and columns:

  • package, version

  • total_lines: all lines in the analysed files.

By type (these four add up to total_lines):

  • code_lines: lines containing code, including code followed by a comment and lines inside multi-line strings.

  • comment_lines: lines containing only a regular (#) comment.

  • roxygen_lines: lines containing only a roxygen (#') comment.

  • blank_lines: empty or whitespace-only lines.

By location (these three add up to total_lines):

  • r_lines: lines in R/.

  • test_lines: lines in tests/.

  • other_lines: lines elsewhere (e.g. data-raw/).

And:

  • function_lines: code lines inside function definitions (a subset of code_lines). Nested functions are counted once.

Details

Lines are classified with R's own parser (utils::getParseData()), so strings that contain # or unbalanced braces are counted correctly, and functions are detected however they are written (<-, =, \(x) lambdas, or anonymous functions inside calls). Files that fail to parse fall back to a line-based heuristic and their function lines are not counted; a warning names each such file.

Only files that R CMD build would ship are analysed, so results for a local folder are comparable with results for a CRAN tarball. In particular, anything listed in .Rbuildignore (often data-raw/) is skipped unless include_ignored = TRUE.

See also

pkg_structure() for file counts, pkg_summary() for both, and pkg_plot() to visualise the result.

Examples

pkg_lines(pkginspectr_example())
#> Counting lines in examplepkg...
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>   package version total_lines code_lines comment_lines roxygen_lines blank_lines
#>   <chr>   <chr>         <int>      <int>         <int>         <int>       <int>
#> 1 exampl… 1.2.3            32         21             2             4           5
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: r_lines <int>, test_lines <int>, other_lines <int>,
#> #   function_lines <int>

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# GitHub repositories and CRAN packages are downloaded and cached
pkg_lines(c("r-lib/cli", "desc"))

# Specific versions, kept across sessions
pkg_lines(c("r-lib/cli@v3.6.0", "cran::desc@1.4.0"), cache = "persistent")
}
